task_instance: Scaffold a minimal Cloudflare Worker using @cloudflare/sandbox@next (1.0 preview) that follows the skill's contract (argv-based sandbox.exec, handle.output(), proxyToSandbox, typed DurableObjectNamespace<Sandbox> binding, wrangler.jsonc container binding), typecheck it against the installed @next types, then run it locally with `wrangler dev` to actually execute `python3 -c "print(2 + 2)"` inside a real sandbox container and verify the JSON response.
blocker_detail: Writing and typechecking the @next Worker code succeeded completely (npm install of @cloudflare/sandbox@next 0.13.0-next.776.1, wrangler, workers-types; `npx tsc --noEmit` passed with 0 errors against the installed preview types). Docker was available and its daemon could be started in this sandbox, and `wrangler dev` did proceed to build the Sandbox container image from node_modules/@cloudflare/sandbox/Dockerfile. However the build's early apk layer (installing ca-certificates/curl into the Alpine-based build stages) needs to fetch from dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org, and the sandbox's egress proxy returns 403 'connect_rejected (organization policy)' for that host (confirmed via curl and via GET http://127.0.0.1:34087/__agentproxy/status, which logs repeated connect_rejected entries for dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org:443 as well as other build-time hosts like pkgs.dev.azure.com and nuget.org). This is an explicit, non-workaroundable organization egress policy denial (per /root/.ccr/README.md: '403/407 ... Do not retry or route around it'), not a missing local tool. It blocked building/running the actual sandbox container and therefore executing sandbox.exec against a live container. Separately, even if the local container build succeeded, shipping/deploying this app for real use would require a Cloudflare account (needs_credentials_or_account), which was out of scope per the safety rules anyway.
evidence: Work directory: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec/cloudflare__skills__sandbox-next/work . Files produced: src/index.ts (Worker using getSandbox/proxyToSandbox/Sandbox export and sandbox.exec(['python3','-c','print(2 + 2)']).output()), wrangler.jsonc (containers/durable_objects/migrations config), tsconfig.json. `npm install @cloudflare/sandbox@next wrangler@latest typescript @cloudflare/workers-types` succeeded (installed @cloudflare/sandbox 0.13.0-next.776.1). `npx tsc --noEmit` exited 0 with no errors after fixing the Env interface to `Sandbox: DurableObjectNamespace<Sandbox>` (matches the skill's non-negotiable API contract, e.g. argv exec + handle.output()). Started dockerd manually (it is present but not running by default); `docker run --rm hello-world` succeeded, proving Docker itself works with network access. `npx wrangler dev --local` correctly detected the container config and began `docker build` of node_modules/@cloudflare/sandbox/Dockerfile, but failed at the `apk add --no-cache ca-certificates curl` layer with 'WARNING: fetching https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/... Permission denied' / TLS certificate errors. Retried a manual `docker build --network host --secret id=wrangler_ca,src=/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt ...` per the sandbox's own documented docker-build proxy workaround; still failed at the same apk layer. Root cause confirmed via `curl -x http://127.0.0.1:34087 https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/...` returning 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' and `curl http://127.0.0.1:34087/__agentproxy/status` showing recentRelayFailures with kind 'connect_rejected' and detail 'gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)' for host dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org:443.
